text.p: These are the leading stories in the Mozambican press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three like-minded Mozambican opposition parties have formed a coalition called the Alliance for Democracy to contest the country's first municipal elections, scheduled for December this year. The three -- the Nationalist Movement, the United Front and the National Convention -- ran separately in parliamentary elections in 1994 and failed to win any seats.

- Opposition deputies in parliament attacked an article in the government's land tenure bill that would grant renewable land titles to Mozambican and foreign investors for periods of up to 50 years. The biggest parliamentary oppostion party, Renamo, wants to reduce the time limit to 25 years.
- The Maputo city court has ordered the seizure of German mine-clearing vehicles on the grounds that the owner has not paid 32 Mozambican workers for the last 10 months.
